svg.title: One scalar, three conditional mass windows
svg.desc: Synthetic numerical example with scalar201.0072764665789, declared double-proton positive ion channel, and10ppm referenced to that scalar. Three possible interpretations yield different neutral monomer mass windows. The tool does not qualify the source mass basis or identify chemicals. A singly charged ion total mass and m/z can agree numerically; a dimer conversion refers to monomer mass.
svg.text: One scalar, three conditional mass windows
Synthetic S = 201.0072764665789 · declared [M+2H]2+ · n = 1, h = 2, z = +2 · 10 ppm
Charge and dimers change the conversion, not the evidence
Charge 2: total ion mass = 2 × precursor m/z. The m/z window scales with |z|.
Dimer [2M+H]+: M = (ion mass − p) / 2. The neutral interpretation always means monomer M.
Charge 1: ion mass and m/z windows coincide. Agreement still cannot qualify the basis.
Candidate counts refer to source positions; equal masses stay separate. Chemical identity remains unmeasured.
PPM denominator is the supplied scalar under each assumed unit; no original reference records or models are used.
Rounded display. JSON reports the implemented binary64 endpoints. Neutral windows do not screen ion feasibility.
